title: The Route Tree
narrativeQuestion: How did people the NFL never planned for find their way onto rosters, and what does Invincible change about Vince Papale's real route? How does this illustrated documentary distinguish evidence from interpretation?

chapters.title: The Vet, 1976
chapters.claim: Papale was a pole vaulter with no college football and two WFL seasons who made the Eagles at 30 after an invited workout. Invincible cut the Bell and invented the walk in tryout.

namedPeople.name: Vince Papale
namedPeople.anchorNote: Vince Papale in January 2009, more than thirty years after his rookie season. Photo: Philip Nelson, Live Streaming Expert (philipnelson.org).

chapters.title: The Odds
chapters.claim: Of 1,000 high school players about 73 play NCAA football and about 1 senior in 1,000 is drafted.

chapters.title: The Route Tree
chapters.claim: Ten routes into the NFL share a few doors: a walk in, a call, a tryout, another league, another sport, a cut, an injury, a program.

chapters.title: Night Train Lane
chapters.claim: An Army veteran walked into the Rams office in 1952 and set the 14 interception record.

namedPeople.name: Dick Lane
namedPeople.anchorNote: Lane is number 81, center right, recovering a fumble against the 49ers, September 3, 1953. Full frame retained; his identity is established by the source caption.

chapters.title: Johnny Unitas
chapters.claim: Cut by the Steelers in 1955, he played sandlot ball for $6 a game until an 80 cent call from Baltimore.

namedPeople.name: Johnny Unitas
namedPeople.anchorNote: Johnny Unitas at Harborplace, Maryland, January 20, 1996. Later portrait, not his 1955 sandlot season.

chapters.title: Rocky Bleier
chapters.claim: Pick 417, wounded in Vietnam in 1969, told he would never play, he won four Super Bowls.

namedPeople.name: Rocky Bleier
namedPeople.anchorNote: Rocky Bleier (left) with Doug Larsen at the National Guard conference in Bismarck, January 24, 2009.

chapters.title: Kurt Warner
chapters.claim: Undrafted and cut, he stocked shelves for $5.50 an hour, then went through arena football and NFL Europe to two MVPs in 1999.

namedPeople.name: Kurt Warner
namedPeople.anchorNote: Kurt Warner speaking in April 2007. Later identity photograph, not a photograph of his grocery work.

chapters.title: Michael Lewis
chapters.claim: A beer truck driver with no college set the 2002 NFL record of 2,432 return yards for his hometown Saints.

namedPeople.name: Michael Lewis
namedPeople.anchorNote: Michael Lewis, the wide receiver and return specialist, with San Francisco on November 18, 2007. This is his later 49ers season, not his Saints debut.

chapters.title: Stephen Neal
chapters.claim: A world champion wrestler with no college football won three Super Bowls at guard.

namedPeople.name: Stephen Neal
namedPeople.anchorNote: Stephen Neal with New England against Washington, August 28, 2009. Later NFL photograph, not the 1999 wrestling final.

chapters.title: Antonio Gates
chapters.claim: A Kent State basketball player became the first Hall of Famer who never played college football.

namedPeople.name: Antonio Gates
namedPeople.anchorNote: Antonio Gates before a San Diego Chargers game, October 30, 2016. Later NFL photograph, not his college basketball years.

chapters.title: Jordan Mailata
chapters.claim: An Australian rugby league prospect who had never played football went 233rd and won Super Bowl LIX.

namedPeople.name: Jordan Mailata
namedPeople.anchorNote: Jordan Mailata visiting Arlington National Cemetery, April 28, 2025. Later portrait, not a scene from his 2018 draft.

chapters.title: Brandon Aubrey
chapters.claim: A software engineer who had never kicked in a game made his first 35 NFL field goals.

namedPeople.name: Brandon Aubrey
namedPeople.anchorNote: Brandon Aubrey playing soccer for Bethlehem Steel FC against Cincinnati, June 13, 2018. A photograph from the sport he left before becoming an NFL kicker.

chapters.title: The Draft Board
chapters.claim: Three of ten were drafted, at 102, 233 and 417. Seven were never drafted, and three of those seven reached the Hall of Fame.

chapters.title: Other Sports
chapters.claim: A Zamboni driver won an NHL game in 2020 and a science teacher struck out a big leaguer in 1999.

chapters.title: Behind the ink
chapters.claim: The Route Tree itself moved from comic universes to a source-led illustrated documentary. Photographs, overpaintings and reconstructions support different kinds of historical claims.

chapters.title: Your Route
chapters.claim: Students map their own goal onto the tree and tie it to one universe with evidence.
